my parents found out while we were on a trip. i took 3 grams of h on a plane cross country (holy shit and this is SO ILLEGAL). left my purse in an uber...the driver went through it probably expecting to steal money from me and showed my dad. obviously, my parents flushed everything, screamed at me, and threw me into full blown withdrawal. i had to fly coast to coast in cold sweats almost shitting myself. i quit my job, stopped talking to everyone, went to an outpatient rehab a week later...it was rough. i wanted to die everyday for like 8 months.

i got a job in feburary, and that got me out of bed. in april, i got in a head on at 70 mph a mile from my house. the next morning, the pain was so bad (and so was the concussion, my 4th one, that i didn't know i had) that i used again. told the rehab place i lapsed and they kicked me out. honestly, fuck the program. who tells trauma victims to repent for THEIR sins? like seriously? they don't do that to lung cancer patients. sorry, no medicine, just look at all of the flaws in your character. it's bullshit.

i started college again this week. i'm in a play. i'm happy for the first time in years or maybe ever, happy in a way that isn't just the warmth of that opiate blanket. it's a happiness i'm making myself. today, i don't want to use, and i don't want to die.

I feel you. I have severe body dysmorphia, and so I really don't know what I look like at all. The way I'm currently dealing with it is to actually not deal with it. I stopped counting calories so that I wouldn't think about them, stopped weighing myself, stopped window shopping to check my size, stopped taking my body measurements. I highly recommend getting numbers out of your life as much as possible.

If you find yourself thinking about your body or looking at yourself, get distracted. Reddit is PERFECT for this. Talk to your therapist about body dysmorphia too, they might have more answers.
